ci-bot: [regression] nightly/perf pipeline detected p95 eventstream latency +62ms vs baseline for rollout v1.12.3, gating failed. details: https://ci.redwood/perf/235801
eli: saw the alert, investigating. initial flame shows a new hotpath: eventpipe -> serialize_toolcall -> small_write_coalesce
tara: link to flame?
eli: sending snippet: ```
# perf summary
p50: +8ms
p95: +62ms
hot functions:
 - serialize_toolcall (44%)
 - kernel_autoselect_slowpath (21%)
 - kv_cache_miss_handler (13%)
```
dmitri: did we change streaming framing or toolcall serialization in the last release?
maya: we merged PR #4789 earlier today — it changed SSE handshake to include an attachment header and moved small-write coalescing to the client-side layer.
eli: that matches. the handshake adds an extra serialize step for toolcall metadata; combined with coalescing it trips kernel_autoselect into a slower kernel for short sequences. also see KV cache hitrate drop: 94% -> 78% on staging.
tara: ouch. staging reproduces?
ci-bot: ci: perf/regression job queued for staging (job id 235801).
dmitri: starting git bisect now to isolate commit. will try quick revert locally.
eli: quick repro (runs a streaming toolcall loop): ```
for i in {1..100}; do 
  curl -N -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
    -d '{"input":"short prompt '.$i'"}' \
    https://api.redwood/run/stream | head -n1; 
done
```
maya: fyi the PR also tweaks the cache key format for toolcall attachments (shorter prefix). could explain kv churn.
dmitri: bisect result: commit f4a3b2 changed framing + kernel hint. reverting f4a3b2 locally drops p95 by ~48ms and restores kv hitrate to ~92%.
eli: good signal. rollout hold recommended. opening revert PR now.
tara: please add canary hold to the release and notify support.
maya: I'll update the release ticket and notify infra to stop the deploy.
eli: i'll run the full perf matrix on the revert PR and attach results. if revert looks clean we'll ship revert and follow up with a smaller fix for batching heuristics. :thumbsup:
dmitri: plan B if revert causes other regressions: we can gate the handshake header behind a feature flag and tweak kernel_autoselect thresholds. but revert is fastest.
tara: thanks team — ping me when revert CI passes. :eyes:
ci-bot: perf/regression: initial staging run posted: https://ci.redwood/PerfRun/235801/results (p95 currently +6ms on revert branch)
eli: excellent, keep thread updated.
